To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MET exon 14 splice site mutations, a potential mechanism for MET overexpression, are present in 5.7% of GI cancers and are associated with overexpression of the MET receptor but rarely with MET gene amplification.

(1) MET exon 14 skipping transcript is a potential actionable mechanism of MET overexpression in GI malignancies; (2) MET exon 13 skipping transcript is not associated with MET overexpression in any malignancies; (3) MET exon 15 skipping transcript is not a potential mechanism of MET over-expression in GI malignancies.
METex14del corresponds with overexpression of the MET protein in GI cancers and can be effectively targeted by several MET inhibitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of MET exon 14 splice site mutations and their impact in the treatment of cancer.
the identification and characterization of a novel METex14del in GI malignancies with the potential of being a new therapeutic target for these cancers.

the development of a new molecular diagnostic test for the presence of the MET exon 14 mutation in patients with cancer, which can be used to identify a subset of patients who may benefit from MET inhibitor therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
METex14del, a rare but unique molecular aberration in GI malignancies, may serve as a potential actionable driver for GI malignancies.
METex14del represents a potential targetable driver mutation in GI tumors.
METex14del, which is present in a subset of GI tumors, corresponds with MET IHC 2+ or greater but not necessarily with MET amplification and is a potential actionable target.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

METex14del, which is a unique molecular alteration present in GI malignancies, can be identified by multiplexed gene expression analysis and can be targeted by MET tyrosine-kinase inhibitors and a monoclanl antibody targeting MET.
MET exon 14 skipping is a potential actionable target in gastrointestinal malignancies.
METex14del may be an important actionable driver mutation in patients with GI malignancies and should be routinely screened in patients with GI cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
METex14del may serve as a potential actionable target in GI malignancies, and that the presence of MET amplification is not required for MET protein over-expression.
